channel_name: Real Vision · Raoul Pal - The journey man
video_title: Raoul Pal: My Entire Macro Framework, Explained
gist: Despite the title, this is mostly a promotional walkthrough of Raoul Pal's self-built GMI/Real Vision dashboards (free, Macro Investing Tool, Pro tiers) rather than a full framework explainer. The embedded macro read: risk-on 'summer' with rising liquidity and expanding business cycle, but tightening financial conditions from a strong dollar as the red-flag tripwire; base-case liquidity cycle end around early 2027, with Pal leaning toward a CapEx-driven 1990s-style elongated supercycle.

insights.claim: Pal's GMI dashboards currently classify the macro regime as 'summer' / risk-on: global liquidity rising, the economy growing and the business cycle in full expansion, signalling a risk-taking environment.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Framework still says stay risk-on; underweighting risk assets fights the regime signal.

insights.claim: Financial conditions have been tightening, largely because of dollar strength, and Pal treats this as the leading warning in his business-cycle 'dominoes' since financial conditions lead global liquidity, which leads markets.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: A tightening FCI is the first domino to watch for a turn in liquidity and then risk assets; the dollar is the swing variable.
insights.quote: Financial conditions have been tightening because of the dollar

insights.claim: The pro portfolio's own tripwire on the financial conditions index is flashing red, so the stance is 'hold' rather than add, with a choppy market despite the intact secular trend.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Signals Pal is not adding aggressively here; a further FCI deterioration would be the trigger to de-risk.
insights.quote: we've got a red one, which is the financial conditions index

insights.claim: Global liquidity has stagnated and been pulled down by a stronger dollar, even though Pal's 'everything code' says the dollar should be falling; he describes the dollar as stuck and diverging from the model.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Dollar/model divergence is the key risk: if the dollar keeps rising, liquidity-driven assets like Bitcoin and Nasdaq lose their tailwind.
insights.quote: The dollar, the everything code should says should be going lower. It's been rising. It is stuck.

insights.claim: Pal estimates the debt refinancing cycle at about 5.6 years, which on the base case would put the end of the current liquidity cycle around early 2027.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete horizon (early 2027) for when the liquidity-cycle top could arrive under the base case.
insights.quote: we think it's about 5.6 years. That would give us till about early '27

insights.claim: Pal's alternative and preferred view is a CapEx-driven supercycle resembling the 1990s, where growth slows somewhat and then re-accelerates, elongating the cycle beyond the 2027 base-case end.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: If right, the cycle runs longer than the refi clock implies, favouring staying long tech/crypto secular trends through a mid-cycle slowdown.
insights.quote: I think we're in a super cycle because of CAPEX

insights.claim: Pal characterises the recent pullback as a mid-cycle correction and says the cycle is most likely elongated; he took no 'lifestyle chips' off the table because markets never reached his 2 standard deviation overbought threshold.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Implies he sees no cycle-top euphoria yet; profit-taking discipline is tied to stretch levels not reached.
insights.quote: So, is this an elongated cycle? Most likely, in my view.

insights.claim: Pal says investors have roughly five years to make as much money as possible, framing a 2030 horizon for the current opportunity window.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Signals a time-bound bullish window; stated in a promotional context for his free report.
insights.quote: I think you've got 5 years to make as much money as possible

insights.claim: The Nasdaq had been flashing 'take profits' for a couple of months after becoming dramatically overbought and was starting to come off that overbought state, with the model saying it is not yet the time to add.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Suggests waiting for a reset toward trend before adding to US tech exposure.
insights.quote: Hey, this is not the time to really add this yet.

insights.claim: Bitcoin's secular trend is confirmed: the everything code (liquidity) says it should go higher and the weekly trend monitor shows it is in trend.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Both liquidity model and price trend align bullish on Bitcoin, the core secular holding.

insights.claim: Commodities have had about a 2 standard deviation move over 3 months and 1.7 standard deviations over a year, which Pal flags as potentially overbought; oil led asset classes over the past year, while Solana then Ethereum led over 6 months.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Commodities look stretched for new entries; momentum leadership has rotated among crypto majors.
insights.quote: Commodities have had a two standard deviation move over the last 3 months.

insights.claim: Pal's macro-seasons read flags small caps as cheap, but he questions whether they are working yet, i.e. value without confirmation.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Potential rotation opportunity into small caps, contingent on trend confirmation.

insights.claim: Sector momentum shows technology leading at almost every horizon in a tech bull market, with healthcare leading over the last week and energy earlier; Coinbase is flagged for extreme volatility and rated hold versus fair value.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Tech remains the leadership trade; healthcare is the short-term rotation to watch.
insights.quote: we're in a technology bull market, so technology wins at almost every level

insights.claim: Retail attention in the Real Vision community has shifted away from Bitcoin, which is 'not exciting to people right now', toward Sui and Tao.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Waning retail excitement in Bitcoin amid an intact trend is a sentiment-contrarian signal; attention is rotating to altcoins.
insights.quote: Bitcoin is not exciting to people right now. Sui seems big right now.

insights.claim: Pal's 'compounding machine' approach books Bitcoin and the Nasdaq as the core secular trends, buying when the market is about 1.5 standard deviations oversold versus trend and trimming (e.g. 20%) at around 2 standard deviations overbought.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: A concrete, rules-based accumulate/trim scheme for secular-trend assets that avoids timing cycles by gut.
insights.quote: You want to buy when the market's oversold one and a half standard deviations. You want to sell when it gets to two standard deviations.

insights.claim: Pal's 'fair value' is not a P/E-type valuation but a trend valuation: where the asset trades versus its own trend and versus where the everything code (liquidity) says it should be.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: Clarifies that Pal's 'cheap/expensive' calls are trend-deviation calls, not fundamental valuation.
insights.quote: Fair value is not a calculation on P ratios or anything that. It's it's a trend valuation model.

insights.claim: The business-cycle 'dominoes' sequence runs financial conditions to global liquidity to markets, and the Nasdaq-versus-global-liquidity correlation remains a core chart; risk is sized using a liquidity supertrend, the business cycle and the weekly trend indicator plus volatility.
insights.speaker: Raoul Pal
insights.so_what: The transmission chain to monitor: FCI first, liquidity second, asset prices last.
